subject: Data from the created plot - is ggplot_build the best way?

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Data from the created plot - is ggplot_build the best way?
parts:
Hi,
I need to get the data from all of the plots I have created. In this case, I have used geom_histogram or geom_boxplot, so I want to know the heights of bars and the box and whisker boundaries. I have seen in posts by others that the function ggplot_build is available to help with this, and does indeed give me the information I need. However, posters have warned using ggplot_build because it was not really intended for this purpose and that it might go away in the future.

So, before I embark on writing code to pull data out using ggplot_build, I am wondering if someone can shed some more light on this concept. Is ggplot_build the best way to do this today? Is there a plan for ggplot_build to go away in the future? Is there a plan to create a different function to provide this data in the future?

Note, I do understand that I could either pre-compute all of the data I have mentioned and plot using that data instead of the raw data or plot the raw data and then post-compute the values I need externally to the plot. However, in both cases that seems to defeat the ease of use of using ggplot to make the plots for you.

Many thanks, and happy new year!
Doug

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Data from the created plot - is ggplot_build the best way?
parts:
> So, before I embark on writing code to pull data out using ggplot_build, I
> am wondering if someone can shed some more light on this concept. Is
> ggplot_build the best way to do this today? Is there a plan for ggplot_build
> to go away in the future? Is there a plan to create a different function to
> provide this data in the future?

It's the best way, if you don't want to precompute the data, but you
need to expect that ggplot_build might change in the future - i.e. it
will be hard to write robust code based on ggplot_build.

> Note, I do understand that I could either pre-compute all of the data I have
> mentioned and plot using that data instead of the raw data or plot the raw
> data and then post-compute the values I need externally to the plot.
> However, in both cases that seems to defeat the ease of use of using ggplot
> to make the plots for you.

If you're going to wrap it in a function, it should be equally easy to
use if you precompute or use ggplot_build, but precomputing will be
much more reliable. (And the next version of ggplot2 should make it
easier to precompute using the build in statistics)
